subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land an internal provider-normalized tool-schema cache for bundled compatibility hooks, and what proof is required before merge?
rationale: The source root cause is clear, but cache lifecycle and invalidation are provider/runtime owner decisions because stale schemas or cached custom-provider behavior could affect existing provider plugins.

options.title: Land a bounded internal cache
options.body: Review and refresh the existing cache PR or an equivalent replacement that caches only known bundled parameter normalizers and proves custom hooks stay fresh.

options.title: Require live provider proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open until a live Google/Gemini or heap-profile reproduction demonstrates the impact and the cache mitigation on a real workload.

options.title: Reject caching for now
options.body: Document disabling tools as the workaround and leave repeated provider normalization as the current runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Land a bounded internal cache
recommendation.body: Review and refresh the existing cache PR or an equivalent replacement that caches only known bundled parameter normalizers and proves custom hooks stay fresh.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and recent provider/runtime performance history make this the strongest available owner signal for the cache lifecycle decision.
